title: 한눈에 ⑦: 내가 본 것 전하기 -더라·-더니·-던데·-더군·-던
objective: By the end, you can choose the right -더- form to tell someone what you saw or felt yourself in the past. You will also avoid the two most common mistakes: using it for your own actions, and mixing up -던 with -(으)ㄴ.
summary: This sheet puts the five recall forms with -더- (-더라, -더니, -던데, -더군, -던) in one table, so you can share something you saw or felt yourself in the past.

task.title: Choose, complete, and check
task.line: Think about who did the action and whether you saw it yourself, then pick the -더- form that fits.

forms.when: You tell a friend something you saw or felt yourself in the past. -더라 is casual. -더라고요 is the polite spoken form.
forms.exampleMeaning: I saw Minsu studying hard at the library.

forms.when: First part: something you saw before. Second part: how it is different now.
forms.exampleMeaning: It was raining this morning, but now it's clear.

forms.when: You saw someone keep doing something, and the second part is what happened because of it. The subject is usually someone else.
forms.example: 동생이 매일 밤 게임을 하더니 시험을 망쳤어요.
forms.exampleMeaning: My brother played games every night, and he did badly on his exam.

forms.when: You share something you saw as background for a suggestion or question. With 요, it can end a sentence softly.
forms.example: 새로 생긴 빵집에 사람이 많던데 우리도 가 볼까요?
forms.exampleMeaning: The new bakery was crowded when I saw it. Shall we go too?

forms.when: You say something you noticed and found new or surprising. It sounds a bit formal, mostly used in speech.
forms.exampleMeaning: I noticed that Korean people walk really fast.

forms.when: It describes a noun with a past action that you did often or did not finish, or with a past state.
forms.means: the N that (someone) used to / was doing
forms.example: 이건 제가 어릴 때 자주 듣던 노래예요.
forms.exampleMeaning: This is a song I often listened to as a child.

watchOut: 내가 밥을 먹더라 (X) → 친구가 밥을 먹더라 (O): -더라 tells what you saw someone else do, not your own action.
나는 매일 운동하더니 건강해졌어요 (X) → 형은 매일 운동하더니 건강해졌어요 (O): with -더니 (result), the subject is usually another person.
어제 다 읽던 책 (X) → 어제 다 읽은 책 (O): -던 means the action was not finished or was repeated. For a finished action, use -(으)ㄴ.
선생님, 그 식당 정말 친절하더라 (X) → 선생님, 그 식당 정말 친절하던데요 (O): -더라 is casual. Use -던데요 or -더라고요 with elders.
exercises: Choose the right form: ① 어제 수진 씨를 만났는데 얼굴이 많이 (안 좋더라 / 안 좋던). ② 오전에는 (덥더니 / 더워서) 저녁에는 쌀쌀해졌어요.
Fill in the blank with -던 (마시다). You stopped drinking it halfway: 아까 제가 ____ 커피 어디 있어요?
Fill in the blank with -더니 (연습하다): 지민 씨가 석 달 동안 매일 ____ 운전을 아주 잘하게 됐어요.
Write O if the sentence is correct and X if it is wrong: ① 나는 어제 숙제를 하더라. ② 그 가게 직원이 정말 친절하던데요. ③ 제가 열심히 공부하더니 합격했어요. ④ 아까 회의실에 아무도 없더군요.
Change it to polite speech for your teacher, using -던데요: 그 책 좀 어렵더라.
Put the words in order to make one sentence: 곳이에요 / 아버지가 / 이 식당이 / 가던 / 자주
answers: ① X ② O ③ X ④ O
그 책 좀 어렵던데요. (또는: 그 책 좀 어렵더라고요.)
이 식당이 아버지가 자주 가던 곳이에요.
